comment: SCP-OUT-039 streaming conformance vectors per §5.4.5. Seven vectors exercise every streaming edge case: non-streaming one-shot, multi-chunk, cancellation, terminal error, recoverable error, sequence gap, and credit exhaustion. Each vector models the control-plane ordering between executor-emitted chunks and receiver-issued credit grants / cancels. The wire-level signature/preimage layer is covered separately by the §5.4.5 chunk_sig and credit_sig fixtures (caveats_binding, SCP-OUTLET-CHUNK-SIG-V1, SCP-OUTLET-CREDIT-V1) — these vectors deliberately omit signatures so they can be replayed against synthetic identities. Per-bridge funnel: all four FFI bridges (PyO3, NAPI, UniFFI Swift/Kotlin, WASM) funnel through scp_runtime::context::outlets::stream (CreditTracker, CancelAckTracker, StreamEscrow, compute_chunks_billed_ref) — the Rust replay validates the runtime path; per-SDK smoke tests assert that each vector produces the expected terminal status through the SDK's InvocationHandle pump. The 'name' field is a stable case identifier; the 'description' is human-readable narrative cross-referenced to the spec.

vectors.name: non_streaming
vectors.description: §5.4.5 'Non-streaming invocation' — a one-shot Action that emits exactly Data(value) followed by End(aggregate). The degenerate two-chunk case the spec collapses to. Models invoke()→sync surface that completes after the End chunk lands.

vectors.name: multi_chunk
vectors.description: §5.4.5 'Per-chunk operator signature' / streaming Query — 10 sequential Data chunks followed by End. Credit window opens at 32 (DEFAULT_CREDIT_WINDOW) so no mid-stream grants are required. Models a paginated Query result set.

vectors.name: cancellation
vectors.description: §5.4.5 'Cancellation and billing boundary' — receiver issues OutletCancel after sequence 3 lands; executor honors with terminal Error{terminal:true} cancel-ack at sequence 4 within stream_cancel_ack_secs window. cancel_ack_seq is pinned at the next-to-emit sequence (4) at cancel arrival; chunks above the ceiling are NOT billed. Terminal status Cancelled per §5.4.5 event-log shape.

vectors.name: error_terminal
vectors.description: §5.4.5 ChunkPayload::Error with terminal=true — executor emits two Data chunks then a terminal Error which immediately closes the stream. Status Error(code) per StreamTerminalStatus. Code SCP-TOOL-6130 (execution.handler-panic) — operator-emitted handler fault.

vectors.name: error_recoverable
vectors.description: §5.4.5 ChunkPayload::Error with terminal=false — executor emits a Data chunk, then a non-terminal Error (informational; stream remains open per §5.4.5), then more Data chunks, then End. Stream completes with terminal status Ok. Models a transient fault the operator surfaces but recovers from (e.g., a downstream timeout that retries internally).

vectors.name: sequence_gap
vectors.description: §5.4.5 'Ordering and gaps' — receiver observes sequences 0, 1, 3 (gap at 2) and MUST cancel the stream with OutletErrorClass::Execution::StreamGap. The expected_error_code follows the §5.4.4 taxonomy slug→code allocation (execution.stream-gap shares SCP-TOOL-6131 with execution.credit-exhausted per the round-5 slug consolidation; the story description's '6134' is reserved/unallocated and predated the consolidation). Receiver-side cancel-and-rerun mitigation per the spec — MLS provides no per-message retransmit primitive.

vectors.name: credit_exhaustion
vectors.description: §5.4.5 'Credit-based backpressure' — receiver sends NO credit grants beyond the initial credit_window of 2. Executor emits 2 Data chunks (consuming all initial credit), credit reaches zero, stream_credit_stall_secs (here 30s, modeled abstractly via the trigger 'credit_stall_fires') elapses without a grant, framework emits the terminal Error{code=SCP-TOOL-6133, terminal=true} cancel-ack-style chunk per CancelAckTracker::credit_stall_payload. Status Error(SCP-TOOL-6133).

chunks.message: credit window remained at zero past stream_credit_stall_secs
